coverage.evidence: package.json:45 names the exact version, "peer-ai-eslint-config": "1.0.0-next.16", with no range operator, which is how its predecessor was pinned too. The lockfile is committed and its diff carries a new integrity hash for each of the three packages that moved, so the bytes installed are fixed: peer-ai-eslint-config sha512-VC0cu6c9qQDr..., peer-ai-standards sha512-XlDD3/8Wo0og..., peer-ai-workflow sha512-vVVKOnugBiDe... npm install -E was used rather than a plain install, so no caret was introduced.

No dependency is added; one devDependency moves 1.0.0-next.15 to 1.0.0-next.16 and two of its own dependencies follow. The reason is in the commit message and the pull request body: next.16 carries Peer AI #235, which stops a reporting-only rule replacing an enforced rule that shares the same ESLint rule, and this project had exactly that shape. Nothing else in the project does that job, since the package is Peer AI's own lint configuration.

Nothing checks dependencies for vulnerabilities, on change or on a schedule. .github/workflows/pr-checks.yml runs verify, a repo-rules guard and gitleaks; .github/workflows/peer-ai.yml runs the Peer AI gate. Neither runs npm audit, there is no scheduled workflow, and no dependency bot is configured. Run by hand at this commit, npm audit reports 19 vulnerabilities: 5 critical, 8 high, 5 moderate, 1 low. No time to fix is set for any severity.

coverage.reason: DEL-07 applies from production, and this project has no production deployment yet. The rule's concern is answered anyway: peer-ai-eslint-config is a devDependency, read only by eslint.config.js, and nothing it brings in reaches the browser bundle.

coverage.evidence: There is no .npmrc in the repository, so installs go to the default public registry, and every one of the three moved packages resolves in package-lock.json to https://registry.npmjs.org/ with an integrity hash. The project publishes nothing of its own under a private scope, so there is no name a public registry could be made to serve instead: @mizaniya/core is a workspace package resolved from packages/core by path, not by name from a registry. Dependency confusion has no surface here.

coverage.reason: DEL-10 applies from production, and nothing is released yet. package-lock.json is a complete list of every direct and indirect dependency with its version and registry, which is what the rule asks for in substance; a generated bill of materials is a release-time artefact and belongs with the deployment work.

coverage.evidence: Read from each package's own metadata in node_modules rather than from memory: peer-ai-eslint-config, peer-ai-standards and peer-ai-workflow all declare license MIT. MIT permits use and redistribution with attribution and imposes nothing on the project's own licensing, so it fits this repository's PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 without conflict. All three are devDependencies, so none is distributed with the product at all.

None of the three packages runs code at install time: their package.json scripts are build and generate only, with no preinstall, install or postinstall hook, read from the installed copies. None is abandoned - all three were published 2026-10-08 as part of the same release. None is a look-alike name: they are the Peer AI packages this project already depends on and whose repository the config names, moving between two versions of the same line. The one install script npm warned about during this install, unrs-resolver's postinstall, comes from eslint-import-resolver-typescript, predates this change, and npm declined to run it.

findings.title: Nothing checks dependencies for vulnerabilities, and 5 critical advisories stand
findings.evidence: A vulnerability published tomorrow in a package already installed here would be found by nobody. Most attacks use advisories that were already public in components nobody updated, and this project would learn of one only if somebody ran npm audit by hand. npm audit at this commit: 19 vulnerabilities, 5 critical, 8 high. Every one is in the build and test toolchain rather than the shipped bundle - eslint-plugin-boundaries through handlebars and micromatch, tailwindcss through chokidar and fast-glob, vite, vitest through tinypool - and none comes from the packages this change moves. The count was 18 with 2 critical on 7 October, so three criticals were published against code already installed here in six days, which is the rule's whole argument. No workflow runs on a schedule and no dependency bot is configured.
findings.fix: Add npm audit to pr-checks.yml and a scheduled workflow that runs it daily, with a severity threshold that fails the build, and set a time to fix per severity. Separate the dev-only tree from the shipped one in what blocks, so a build-tool advisory does not block a merge that ships nothing.

summary: Pass at the project's blocking level, one high finding open. The change is clean: exact pin, committed lockfile with fresh integrity hashes, MIT licences read from the packages, public registry, no install scripts, reason recorded. DEL-03 fails and not because of this change - nothing watches dependencies, and npm audit reports 19 vulnerabilities, 5 critical, all dev toolchain, none shipped, none from this bump.
